svg.title: Remove cubes with exactly 3 face-neighbors: what survives in two blocks
svg.desc: A solid block of small cubes is thinned one cube at a time. You may remove a cube only if it shares exactly three faces with remaining cubes. Only shared faces count as touching; touching at a corner or edge does not count. Two results are shown as stacks of slices. The 2 by 3 by 9 block ends with 17 survivors, and the 3 by 3 by 6 block ends with 15 survivors. In both cases no two survivors share a face. Filled squares are cubes that remain and empty squares are cubes that were removed. Both outcomes were predicted to be impossible, and these exact results show that they do happen.

g.text: Start: a solid block of small cubes. No two survivors share a face.
Both results below were predicted to be impossible — here they are.
Each mini-grid is one flat slice through the block.
